description: Warnings, timeouts, and notes are stored as records against the member they were given to. Each record stores the moderator who gave it, the date it was given, and the reason provided. Records can be viewed at any time with the records command, and deleted individually or all at once.

description:
A member can have up to `50` records per server. Once a member hits the limit, warnings and timeouts will still be applied, but will no longer be saved as records, and new notes cannot be added.

Kicks, bans, and purges are not stored as records, but are still logged.

When a member is warned, timed out, kicked, or banned, Wynem sends them a DM telling them what happened, along with the reason if one was provided. Members with their DMs closed simply will not receive the message. Notes are the exception: members are never told about their notes.

description.text: How to use the moderation suite

tabs.name: Warning members
content: To warn a member, use the <command:warn [member] [reason]|warn member:[member] reason:[reason]> command. The reason is optional, and can be up to `512` characters long. You need the `Moderate Members` permission to use this command.
For example: <command:warn @TheAnnoying Spamming in chat|warn member:@TheAnnoying reason:Spamming in chat>
The warning is saved as a record, and the member is sent a DM telling them they were warned, along with the reason and their new warning total.

tabs.name: Timing out members
content: To time out a member so that they cannot type or speak, use the <command:timeout [member] [duration] [reason]|timeout member:[member] duration:[duration] reason:[reason]> command. Both you and Wynem need the `Moderate Members` permission.

The duration is optional and defaults to `10` minutes, with a maximum of `28` days. See the [Duration Formatting](/features/durations) feature for the formats you can use. The reason is also optional, and can be up to `512` characters long.
For example: <command:timeout @TheAnnoying 3d Spamming in chat|timeout member:@TheAnnoying duration:3d reason:Spamming in chat>
The timeout is saved as a record, and the member is sent a DM telling them they were timed out, along with the length, the reason, and their new timeout total.
If the member is already timed out, you will be asked to confirm before the new timeout is applied.

data.description:
<@TheAnnoying> is already timed out, are you sure you want to time them out again?

This will extend the timeout by `3 days` and add a new log

tabs.name: Ending timeouts
content: To end the timeout of a member who is currently timed out, use the <command:endtimeout [member] [reason]|moderation endtimeout member:[member] reason:[reason]> command. Both you and Wynem need the `Moderate Members` permission.
Ending a timeout does not remove the original timeout record. If the member is not timed out, you will get an error instead.

tabs.name: Kicking members
content: To kick a member from the server, use the <command:kick [member] [reason]|kick member:[member] reason:[reason]> command. The reason is optional, and can be up to `512` characters long. Both you and Wynem need the `Kick Members` permission.
You will be prompted to confirm you want to kick the member.

data.description: Are you sure you want to kick <@TheAnnoying>?

content: After confirming, the member is sent a DM telling them they were kicked, and is then kicked from the server.
Kicks are not stored as records, but are still logged with the `moderation-kick` log type. Administrators cannot be kicked unless you are the server owner.

tabs.name: Banning members
content: To ban a member from the server, use the <command:ban [member] [reason]|ban member:[member] reason:[reason]> command. The reason is optional, and can be up to `512` characters long. You need the `Ban Members` permission, and Wynem needs the `Ban Members` and `Kick Members` permissions. Users who are not in the server can also be banned.
You will be prompted to confirm you want to ban the member.

data.description: Are you sure you want to ban <@TheAnnoying>?

content: Pressing `Ban` sends the member a DM telling them they were banned, and then bans them. If a ban appeal link is configured, the DM also includes an `Appeal ban` button. See the [Ban Appeals](/features/ban-appeals) feature.

data.title: You have been banned from `Ewan's Server`

content: The `Compromised account` option is for members whose accounts have been hacked, and is only offered for members who are in the server. Instead of a permanent ban, Wynem sends the member an account security alert, bans them while deleting their recent message history, and then immediately unbans them, effectively converting the ban into a kick.

content: Bans are not stored as records, but are still logged with the `moderation-ban` log type. Administrators cannot be banned unless you are the server owner.

tabs.name: Unbanning users
content: To unban a banned user, use the <command:unban [user] [reason]|unban user:[user] reason:[reason]> command. Both you and Wynem need the `Ban Members` permission. The slash command autocompletes the user from the server's ban list.
Unbans are logged with the `moderation-unban` log type. If the user is not banned, you will get an error instead.

tabs.name: Adding notes
content: To add a note to a member, use the <command:addnote [member] [note]|moderation addnote member:[member] note:[note]> command. The note is required, and can be up to `512` characters long. You need the `Moderate Members` permission.

content: To view the moderation records for a member, use the <command:records [member]|moderation records member:[member]> command. You need the `Moderate Members` permission.

content: Records are shown `5` to a page. If a member has more than `5` records, arrow buttons appear so you can move between the pages.
If the member has no records, you will be told instead.
To delete records, press the red bin button. A modal will appear where you can enter the ID of the record to delete, shown under each record, or `ALL` to delete every record.

tabs.name: Purging messages
content: To bulk delete messages from a channel, use the <command:purge [count] [member]|purge count:[count] member:[member]> command. The count is optional and defaults to `5`, with a maximum of `99`. Both you and Wynem need the `Manage Messages` permission.
For example: <command:purge 10|purge count:10>
The confirmation message deletes itself after a few seconds.
You can also provide a member to only delete their messages. Wynem searches through the last `100` messages in the channel for messages from that member.
Purges are logged with the `moderation-purge` log type. Messages that are over two weeks old cannot be purged.
